children.text: jāraṇāṃ vivakṣuḥ prathamaṃ tadbhedān āha varavārtikaiḥ śreṣṭharasaśāstratattvajñair iti trirūpā tribhedā jāraṇā nirdiṣṭā proktā ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to speak of <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion), first he states its divisions. "By the excellent expositors" means "by the foremost knowers of the principles of <s>rasaśāstra</s>." Thus <s>jāraṇā</s> is described, stated, as threefold, with three divisions.

children.text: kāni trīṇi rūpāṇi garbhe cāraṇaṃ garbhe drāvaṇaṃ garbhe jāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: What are the three forms? <s>cāraṇa</s> (feeding or charging) in the <s>garbha</s> (interior), <s>drāvaṇa</s> (liquefaction) in the <s>garbha</s>, and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) in the <s>garbha</s>.
The word <s>garbha</s> is to be connected everywhere.
The sense is: <s>garbhacāraṇa</s> (internal cāraṇa), <s>garbhadrāvaṇa</s> (internal liquefaction), and <s>garbhajāraṇa</s> (internal digestion).

children.text: punar bhūyo jāraṇā iti dvividhā dviprakārā proktā kathitā ||
children.translated_text: Again, furthermore, <s>jāraṇā</s> is said, declared, to be twofold, of two kinds.
What is that twofoldness? <s>nirmukhā</s> (without a mouth) and <s>samukhā</s> (with a mouth).

children.text: jāraṇālakṣaṇaṃ yathā drutagrāsaparīṇāmo viḍayantrādiyogataḥ jāraṇetyucyate tasyāḥ prakārāḥ santi koṭiśaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>jāraṇā</s> is as follows: "The transformation of the molten <s>grāsa</s> (feed or portion), through the use of <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline reagent), apparatuses, and the like, is called <s>jāraṇā</s>; its varieties exist by the crores," thus.
